label: owner-decided
detail: Owner ruling, before R4 (owner-decided 2026-11-11, ~13:40 CST): an exploratory R5 after R4. R5 is exploratory and outside the pre-registration. It was added after R0 to R3's results were seen, and before R4. It enters no pass-rule count, no coverage count, no control label and no README section 3 row. It gets its own section in summary.md, headed as exploratory and stating when and why it was added. Why: on 2026-10-30 the failed reporting and QA starts came after a stretch of edge questions that kept the gateway and orchestrator warm while reporting and QA went cold. In R0 to R4 all six services start cold together. R5 reproduces the 10-30 condition: a cold reporting and QA start behind a warm gateway and orchestrator. Procedure. T is R4's last answer, from the gateway log. Do not run G-CLOSE after R4; ops-db stays running until R5 ends. E1 at about T+5 min: 'How's the Southeast doing?'. E2 at about T+12 min: 'What will revenue be next quarter?'. Typed in the same page with no reload. After each, confirm from the logs that it reached only the gateway and orchestrator: route ambiguous or out_of_scope, no request to reporting or QA, QA not applicable. If either reached reporting or QA, tell the owner before going on. Gate G-R5, at T+20 min or later: read the last request to each service. Reporting and QA must be 20 minutes or more idle, counted from their own last request (QA's is R4's Q3 verification). The gateway and orchestrator must be warm: last request under 10 minutes ago and no shutdown line since. Print the six timestamps and say which conditions hold. If the gateway or orchestrator has gone cold, say so: then R5 tests the same thing as R1 to R4, and the owner decides whether to ask. After the owner's go, Q1 only: 'What was SLA compliance in the Northeast last month?', typed in the same page with no reload. The same retry rule applies: a degraded or 'Not verified' answer gets one retry within 30 s. Evidence: wait 2 minutes, run the committed extractor on R5's read, print the start table and the question table. Any failed, indeterminate or over-60 s start gets the full README 2e capture. Caps: R5 counts toward the session totals: at most 4 questions (E1, E2, Q1, one retry), about 8 model calls, under $0.01. If R5 would cross a session cap, it is not started. The 4-hour limit still ends at 21:46:18Z. After R5: G-CLOSE, then G-REC. The status line comes from R0 to R4 alone. If R5 shows a failure, the owner decides at G-REC whether to add one separate sentence, labelled 'Exploratory R5 (outside the pre-registration)'.

detail: Two adjustments to the R5 ruling (owner-decided, before G-R4). 1) Timing: a later E2 keeps the gateway and orchestrator warmer at G-R5, not colder; the risk is an E2 that comes too early. New schedule: E1 at about T+6, E2 at about T+15, G-R5 at T+20 or later (gateway and orchestrator about 5 minutes idle at the gate). E2 must come no earlier than T+11, and always before Q1. T is R4's last answer from the gateway log. 2) E1 becomes 'What's the weather in New York today?' in place of 'How's the Southeast doing?'. E2 stays 'What will revenue be next quarter?'. On 2026-10-30 both were routed out_of_scope and declined: one model call each, QA not applicable (docs/deploy-window-log.md rows P1 and 5; read by the assistant 2026-11-11 at lines 605-606). 'Southeast' is the riskier choice: FR-03 is unmet and routing is not deterministic (L-17), so it could be best-fit routed to reporting, which would spoil R5. Everything else in the R5 ruling stands. Assistant correction: the assistant's earlier point 1 had the direction reversed (an E2 later than T+14 does not break the gateway/orchestrator idle condition; an E2 earlier than T+11 does, because at T+20 they would be over 10 minutes idle).
